title: Negotiating Through the Body’s Tissue Maze
content: Inflammation is one of our body’s key defense mechanisms. When infection or injury occurs, localized tissue migratory cells (derived from white blood cells) recognize the damage and stimulate an inflammatory response. Among the stimulated responses, other white blood cells in the blood quickly extravasate out of the blood vessels into the surrounding tissue and migrate to the damaged area [1]. Once they reach their target, they participate in several protective functions. The faster the white blood cells get to their target site, the faster they can begin the healing process. Thus, the ability to rapidly move through tissue is a key requirement of these amoeboid white blood cells.
